messages.subject: scale_x_date minor breaks question
parts:
Hi: I am trying to find the equivalent to:
## Version 0.8.9
df <- data.frame(
date = seq(Sys.Date(), len=100, by="1 day")[sample(100, 50)],
price = runif(50))
df <- df[order(df$date), ]
dt <- qplot(date, price, data=df, geom="line")
dt + scale_x_date(major="months", minor="week", format="%B")
with the dev_version.

## Version 0.9
#I want my gridlines to appear by week( 4 between each month)
df <- data.frame(
date = seq(Sys.Date(), len=100, by="1 day")[sample(100, 50)],
price = runif(50))
df <- df[order(df$date), ]
dt <- qplot(date, price, data=df, geom="line")

## Here I get biweekly gridlines
dt + scale_x_date(breaks=date_breaks("month"),labels =
date_format("%b"))

Tried scale_x_continuous() without success

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: scale_x_date minor breaks question
parts:
This is a really weird problem, and I'm not sure what's causing it.
Function arguments should be evaluated in the environment in which
they are created. It's possible the problem occurs because [ is a
primitive function and so behaves a little different.

The fix is to force the evaluation of range before it gets passed to [

discard <- function(x, range = c(0, 1)) {
force(x)

x[x >= range[1] & x <= range[2]]
}

and similar for all the other bounds function. I'm starting teaching
today, so I don't have time to fix it right now, but a patch to scales
would be appreciated, or I'll try to get to it later in the week.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: scale_x_date minor breaks question
parts:
Please see also
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/351#issuecomment-3416522

scales also has `censor` function that is very similar with `discard`.
I think these functions can be integrated as:

censor <- function (x, range = c(0, 1), drop = FALSE)
{
x <- ifelse(x >= range[1] & x <= range[2], x, NA)
if (drop) x[!is.na(x)]
else x
}

--

2012/1/11 Hadley Wickham <had...@rice.edu>:

> This is a really weird problem, and I'm not sure what's causing it.
> Function arguments should be evaluated in the environment in which
> they are created.  It's possible the problem occurs because [ is a
> primitive function and so behaves a little different.
>
> The fix is to force the evaluation of range before it gets passed to [
>
> discard <- function(x, range = c(0, 1)) {
>  force(x)
>  x[x >= range[1] & x <= range[2]]
> }
>
> and similar for all the other bounds function.  I'm starting teaching
> today, so I don't have time to fix it right now, but a patch to scales
> would be appreciated, or I'll try to get to it later in the week.
>
> Hadley
